generator.params.thorns.why: Every bud of a leafy cactus sits in an areole of spines, in its leaf's axil.

generator.params.areole_spines.why: An old areole carries as many spines as its flora counts at most.

generator.params.areole_first.why: A new areole on a young branch carries as many spines as its flora counts there, on the average, or the fewest it counts.

generator.params.thorn_length.why: Floras give the longest spines; the program draws each spine 0.6 to 1.2 times thorn_length.

generator.program.note: The genus's own program, on the broadleaf base: a leafy shrub or tree whose buds sit in areoles of spines.

rules.note: The leafy cacti's areoles drawn from the spine counts and lengths their floras give.

traits.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (read on eFloras 2026-10-19), Pereskia: Stems straight or zig-zag. Spines 1-12 per areole. Flowers from areoles of new growth; outer tepals often greenish, colored near margins; inner tepals white, yellow, orange-red, red, pink to purplish; stamens 50-100 in small-flowered species, to 300 in large-flowered species; stigma lobes 3-20. Flowers from the areoles of new growth, so at the tips of the season's shoots; the stems woody and unribbed (Flora of China: 'Branches terete').
